title: His Gold Seal Said "Emperor" — and a Persian Box Beside It | Buried Empire P2 · 文帝行玺
description:
A vassal king cast a gold seal that called himself Emperor — and in the same tomb sat a Persian silver box. Guangzhou, 2,000 years ago.

The 文帝行玺 seal is the largest Western Han gold seal ever found: 148.5 g, ~98% gold, topped with a coiled dragon. Qin and Han emperors used white jade with tiger knobs — the second king of Nanyue broke that rule and styled himself “Emperor Wen,” even though Nanyue was a Han vassal. Beside it lay a flat silver box with garlic-petal chasing — West-Asian, almost certainly Persian and imported by sea. Chinese craftsmen later welded on a knob and a bronze foot and reused it as a pill box.

🧭 Expert Tip: Both are in the Museum of the Mausoleum of the Nanyue King (南越王博物院), Guangzhou — one ticket, and the maritime-trade gallery explains how a Persian box reached the South China coast.

一枚敢称"帝"的金印，一只波斯银盒——两千年前的广州，就是海上丝路的起点。
